outcomes.text: *Students will use critical thinking to recognize the rigorous standards of scientific theories by:
describing the steps and principles involved in the scientific method.
evaluating different methods of measurement of natural phenomena.
*Students will analyze and synthesize earth science data to draw scientifically valid conclusions by:
identifying rocks and minerals and their properties.
reading and interpreting topographic and geologic maps.
defining the processes that shape the Earth’s surface.
explaining the ways in which geologic materials are dated.
defining the nature of sea water with respect to its chemistry and motion within the ocean basins of the Earth.
describing the structure of our solar system.
explaining the nature of the Earth Moon system
*Students will recognize the different time scales associated with different earth processes by:
evaluating the theoretical causes of major evolutionary and extinction events.
distinguishing mountain building, rifting and other events with respect to the forces that produced them.
memorizing the geologic time scale and placing events in their proper place on this scale.
charting the origin of the universe and our solar system.
*Students will effectively describe interactions between humans and the earth’s spheres by:
comparing and contrasting different types of marine life relative to each other.
analyzing the different features on the ocean floor.
analyzing the history of astronomical thought.
*Students will apply their understanding of earth science principles to complex global and local issues by:
explaining the different ways in which the atmosphere is measured.
labeling and describing components of weather maps.
recognizing how Earth's climate system functions and changes.

assignments.title: Historical Figures in the Geosciences: Focus on Minorities and Women
assignments.instructions:
Research a historical geoscientist, describe their contribution, reflect on representation, and reply to two classmates.

- A biographical paragraph and a few sentences about representation are required.
- Describe observations, measurements, maps, fossils, or other evidence if available in the source.
- Include a reference and two thoughtful replies.

assignments.title: Geologic Time Scale Concept Sketch
assignments.instructions:
Place ten dated events on a geologic time scale and explain the possible causes of two mass extinctions.

- Include ten named events with dates and appropriate time intervals.
- Explain possible causes of the end-Permian and K–T/K–Pg extinctions.
- A hand-drawn or digital sketch is submitted; research is allowed.

assignments.title: Yellowstone Hotspot Lab
assignments.instructions:
Use a hotspot map to measure distance, calculate plate speed, interpret plate direction, compare eruption styles, and upload Yellowstone’s current status.

- Questions 1–4: find the oldest volcanic center, measure its distance with the 100 km scale bar, calculate speed in km/Ma, and convert to cm/year.
- Questions 5–8: use the age pattern and north arrow to describe overall, earlier, and recent plate directions and judge whether the path was straight.
- Questions 9–10: compare Hawaiian (basaltic) and Yellowstone (rhyolitic) explosive potential using silica, viscosity, gas, and crust type.
- Question 11: upload a screenshot of the latest USGS Yellowstone alert level, aviation color code, and update date.

assignments.title: Plate Boundary Concept Sketches
assignments.instructions:
Draw three plate boundaries and explain two additional convergence types, linking motion to features and real plate pairs.

- Draw oceanic divergent, continental–oceanic convergent, and transform boundaries.
- Label movement and features; give a location and both plate names for each sketch.
- Explain continental–continental and oceanic–oceanic convergence in writing.

assignments.title: Science or Snake Oil?
assignments.instructions:
Propose a testable hypothesis, investigation methods, and evidence that would support or challenge a claim; reply to two peers.

- Select a specific claim and devise a falsifiable hypothesis.
- Describe observations, measurements, comparisons or controls, and alternative explanations.
- Propose the investigation without carrying it out, and evaluate two classmates’ methods.

assignments.title: Groundwater Concept Sketch for County Commissioners
assignments.instructions:
Create a one-page handout explaining nearby wells going dry and coastal saltwater intrusion under heavy pumping.

- Show water tables before and after pumping, wells, cones of depression, and flow arrows.
- Show the coastal freshwater–saltwater transition and saltwater movement toward a well.
- Explain both community consequences in plain language and cite sources; no live presentation is required.
